title: He lived in a cave with no clocks and lost 25 days
description:
In July 1962 French scientist Michel Siffre spent two months 130 m underground with no clock, calendar or sun. Counting to 120 took him five minutes, and when his team ended the experiment on 14 September he thought it was 20 August. His body still kept a near-daily rhythm. Harvard later found that switching on lamps resets the body clock in experiments like these; measured properly, your internal day is 24 hours 11 minutes, and light sets it.

Sources:
- Caveman: An Interview with Michel Siffre (Joshua Foer), Cabinet issue 30, Summer 2008 — Cabinet Magazine: https://www.cabinetmagazine.org/issues/30/foer.php
- Michel Siffre, scientist who explored solitude deep within caves, dies at 85 — The Boston Globe (Washington Post obituary): https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/09/04/world/michel-siffre-scientist-solitude-deep-within-caves-dies-85/
- Michel Siffre — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_Siffre
- Human biological clock set back an hour — Harvard Gazette (Harvard University): https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/1999/07/human-biological-clock-set-back-an-hour/
- Circadian Rhythms fact sheet — National Institute of General Medical Sciences (NIH): https://www.nigms.nih.gov/education/fact-sheets/Pages/circadian-rhythms.aspx

The 25 days and the 24.5-hour cycle are Siffre's own account. Michel Siffre is named, not depicted. The clocks change on 25 October (UK) and 1 November (US). The characters are cartoons, not medical advice. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro-82M). Music generated with ACE-Step 1.5; Some sound effects generated with Stable Audio Open (Stability AI).
